newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London edge lower on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London edge lower on U.S. data.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London nudged lower on Friday after strong U.S inflation data weighed on Wall Street and raised prospects for further U.S. interest rate hikes, traders said.
"When the figures came out, the (U.S. long) bond went weaker, we went weaker and the Street opened up obviously quite weakly and we went even weaker on that," one trader said.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index slipped 80.27 points, or 0.64 percent to end the day at 12,436.33 points.

"The market's had a good rally over the last few days, but now there's this implication of higher interest rates which is bad for the Hong Kong property market, so I think we could be in for a nasty day on Monday," another trader said.

The U.S. data showed producer prices slipped 0.1 percent overall, but there was a surprise jump of 0.4 percent in the core U.S. inflation rate for March, in addition to a 0.2 percent rise in retail sales.
Traders said there was little activity in the morning in London as investors held back ahead of the U.S. data and afterwards London experienced a knock-on effect from a softer Wall Street.
"There were no real features in London's Hong Kong stocks, basically it was a mark-down across the board and there wasn't a lot of turnover in the day here," a trader said.
